questions.stem: A company will redeploy 200 laptops with SSDs and must prove that each was erased. Which method BEST fits?

options.text: A drive wipe with firmware secure erase and a report
options.rationale: Correct: reliable on SSDs, reusable, and documented.

options.text: A multi-pass overwrite of each drive's sectors
options.rationale: Allows reuse, but overwriting is less reliable on SSDs.

options.text: Degaussing each SSD before reissue
A quick format on each laptop's drive

questions.explanation: A drive wipe is a tool-driven erase of the whole drive (wipe utilities, firmware secure erase, cryptographic erase), often with verification. It is automated and reportable and supports reuse.
questions.discriminator_tested: Drive wipe: automated, reportable, supports reuse.

questions.stem: A defense contractor plans to degauss its failed SSDs before disposal. Which answer is BEST?

options.text: It doesn't work on SSDs; shred them
Degaussing takes too long for large batches
options.rationale: Time isn't the problem; it doesn't work at all.

options.text: The SSDs must be documented first
options.rationale: Documenting is good practice, but the method itself fails.

options.text: Degaussing leaves SSDs reusable
options.rationale: Degaussing, where it works, destroys drives.

questions.explanation: Physical destruction means shredding, crushing, incineration, or degaussing (magnetic media). It is the most certain method and leaves the drive unusable; degaussing doesn't work on SSDs.

questions.stem: What BEST explains why an untested backup is described as 'unproven'?

options.text: No one knows it can actually be restored
options.rationale: Correct: only a restore test proves a backup works.

options.text: It may be older than the last change
options.rationale: Possibly, but even a current backup is unproven until restored.

options.text: It is stored without encryption at rest
It might be stored at another site

questions.explanation: Data backups are copies of data for recovery after loss, failure, or ransomware. An untested backup is unproven, and offline or offsite copies resist ransomware.

questions.stem: Which two are examples of regulatory compliance requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: PCI DSS rules for handling card data
HIPAA rules for patient health information
The company's own password policy
An internal acceptable use policy
A vendor's recommended configuration baseline
options.rationale: A recommendation, not a legal or industry mandate.

questions.explanation: Regulatory compliance means meeting external legal and industry requirements for handling data (for example HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR). It is externally imposed, unlike internal policy.

questions.stem: What BEST explains why BYOD gives a company less control than organization-owned devices?

options.text: The employee owns the device and its personal data
options.rationale: Correct: ownership limits control and raises privacy concerns.

options.text: BYOD devices come in many makes and models
options.rationale: True and a challenge, but ownership is the root of it.

options.text: BYOD devices are barred from MDM enrollment
Company-owned devices tend to be newer

questions.explanation: BYOD means employee-owned devices; organization-owned devices are under full organizational control. Ownership drives how much control and privacy there is.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes how MDM relates to configuration management, app distribution, and data encryption on mobile devices?

options.text: MDM is the platform that manages those three
options.rationale: Correct: they are capabilities it enforces.

options.text: MDM is another name for configuration management
options.rationale: Configuration management is one thing MDM does.

options.text: They are separate products that replace MDM
options.rationale: They are features delivered through MDM.

options.text: MDM handles encryption and nothing else

questions.explanation: MDM is a central platform to enroll, configure, and enforce policy on mobile devices (remote lock and wipe). Configuration management, app distribution, and data encryption are things it manages.
questions.discriminator_tested: MDM is the platform; the others are what it manages.

questions.stem: Admins change server settings directly whenever they like, with no record, and the servers slowly diverge from one another. What is MOST clearly missing?

options.text: An approved baseline under change control
options.rationale: Correct: it keeps configurations consistent and drift visible.

options.text: Documentation of each change
options.rationale: Part of it, but without a baseline there's nothing to compare against.

options.text: A faster patch deployment process
More powerful server hardware

questions.explanation: Configuration management maintains consistent, documented, approved configurations (baselines) under change control, which detects configuration drift.
questions.discriminator_tested: Baseline plus change control detects drift.

questions.stem: Staff phones keep installing a malicious flashlight app from a third-party store. Which MDM control BEST stops this?

options.text: An app allow list from a managed app store
options.rationale: Correct: governs where apps may come from.

options.text: Remote wipe of infected phones
options.rationale: Cleans up afterwards, but doesn't stop the installs.

options.text: Encrypting the storage on each phone
Requiring a stronger Wi-Fi passphrase

questions.explanation: App distribution controls which apps are installed and from where (a managed app store, allow and block lists). It governs software sources on managed devices.

questions.stem: A laptop with a fully encrypted drive is stolen from a car while powered off. What is the MOST likely outcome for its data?

options.text: It stays unreadable to the thief without the key
options.rationale: Correct: the disk can't be read without the key.

options.text: It is protected while the laptop is powered off
options.rationale: True, but it doesn't say what the thief can do.

options.text: The device can be wiped remotely
options.rationale: That is MDM, and the laptop may never come online.

options.text: The thief can read it by moving the drive
options.rationale: Moving an encrypted drive doesn't decrypt it.

questions.explanation: Data encryption protects data on the device, for example with full-disk encryption. A lost or stolen device doesn't expose readable data.
questions.discriminator_tested: A lost or stolen device doesn't expose readable data.

questions.stem: A PC is badly infected, and the business needs it back today with high confidence that it is clean. What is the BEST recovery approach?

options.text: Reimage it from a known-good image and restore data
options.rationale: Correct: returns it to a known-good state.

options.text: Run several antimalware scans until clean
options.rationale: Might work, but can't give the same confidence.

options.text: Use a System Restore point from last week
Reboot it into safe mode and keep using it

questions.explanation: Endpoint recovery restores an endpoint to a known-good state (restore from backup, reimage, rebuild); it is recovery after a problem, while protection tries to prevent it.

questions.stem: An EDR agent watches process behavior on each laptop and can kill suspicious processes. Which threat does it BEST address?

options.text: Malware running on the endpoint itself
options.rationale: Correct: detective and responsive control on the device.

options.text: A failed hard drive losing data
Rogue devices joining the corporate network
options.rationale: NAC and IP scanning address that.

options.text: Lost laptops exposing their data

questions.explanation: Endpoint protection is the controls on the device itself: antimalware, host-based firewall, host intrusion detection, and EDR. They are preventive and detective controls on the endpoint.
questions.discriminator_tested: Endpoint protection = controls on the device itself.

questions.stem: A salesperson's laptop hasn't connected to the office network in two months. What BEST explains why cloud-based endpoint protection suits it?

options.text: It updates and reports over the internet, from anywhere
It uses threat intelligence from many customers
options.rationale: A real benefit, but not why it suits an off-network laptop.

options.text: It works without any internet connection
It scans when the laptop is on the office LAN
options.rationale: The laptop is never on the LAN.

questions.explanation: Cloud-based protection delivers or analyzes endpoint security through the cloud (cloud signatures, threat intelligence, a central console). It gives fast updates and off-network coverage but needs connectivity.

questions.stem: An antivirus console has shown 'No threats detected' for a server for a month. What should an analyst MOST importantly check before trusting that?

options.text: That scans ran and definitions were current
options.rationale: Correct: a clean result means little otherwise.

options.text: That the server is still powered on and online
options.rationale: Worth knowing, but scan health is the key check.

options.text: That the firewall logs agree
options.rationale: Firewall logs don't confirm scan health.

options.text: That the server's disk is encrypted

questions.explanation: Reviewing scan logs means examining antimalware and vulnerability scan results for detections, failures, and patterns. A clean log doesn't prove safety; check that scans ran and definitions were current.
questions.discriminator_tested: Check that scans ran and definitions were current.

questions.stem: In the malware remediation process, which step comes immediately after disabling System Restore?

options.text: Remediate: update antimalware, scan, and remove
Quarantine the system from the network
Re-enable Restore and create a point
Educate the user about safe habits

questions.explanation: The malware remediation process has seven ordered steps: identify and verify symptoms; quarantine; disable System Restore; remediate; schedule scans and run updates; re-enable System Restore and create restore points; educate users.

questions.stem: Which two are common symptoms that suggest a malware infection? (Choose two.)

options.text: Antivirus that is disabled and won't restart
Browser searches redirected to odd sites
A backup job that failed because the disk was full
A slow login caused by a busy DC
A new monitor not being detected

questions.explanation: Identifying and verifying malware symptoms means gathering signs (slowness, pop-ups, redirects, disabled antivirus, unknown processes) and confirming malware. It is the first step: confirm before acting.

questions.stem: What BEST explains why quarantine comes before cleaning an infected PC?

options.text: It stops the spread while you clean it
It is the second step in the process
options.rationale: True, but it doesn't say why.

options.text: It removes the malware from memory
It restores the PC from a clean backup

questions.explanation: Quarantining infected systems means isolating them from the network (disconnecting or moving them to an isolated VLAN). It stops the spread before cleaning.

questions.stem: A technician cleans malware but forgot to disable System Restore first. Later, a user rolls the PC back to last week's restore point. What is the MOST likely result?

options.text: The malware returns from the old restore point
options.rationale: Correct: the restore point preserved it.

options.text: The PC goes back to last week's state
options.rationale: True, but it misses that last week's state includes the malware.

options.text: The restore fails, since scanning deleted it
The malware is removed a second time
options.rationale: Nothing removes it; it comes back.

questions.explanation: Disable System Restore before cleaning so malware in old restore points isn't preserved; restore points can hold malware.

questions.stem: Before scanning an infected PC, the technician updates the antimalware definitions. What BEST explains why?

options.text: Old definitions may not recognize this malware
Updates are part of the remediation step
options.rationale: True, but it doesn't say why.

options.text: Updating disables System Restore automatically
Updates quarantine the PC automatically

questions.explanation: Remediating infected systems means updating antimalware, scanning, and removing the malware, using safe mode or rescue media when needed. Use current definitions.

questions.stem: Which action belongs to the 'schedule scans and run updates' step of malware remediation?

options.text: Patching apps and the OS; scheduling scans
options.rationale: Correct: closes the hole and keeps checking.

options.text: Creating a fresh restore point
Disconnecting the PC from the network
Training the user to spot phishing

questions.explanation: Scheduling scans and running updates means patching the OS and applications, updating signatures, and scheduling recurring scans. It closes the hole that let the malware in.
questions.discriminator_tested: Closes the hole that let the malware in.

questions.stem: After cleaning, a technician re-enabled System Restore and created a restore point before verifying the PC was clean. The malware later came back from that point. What BEST describes what went wrong?

options.text: It was turned on before the PC was clean
options.rationale: Correct: the new restore point captured the malware.

options.text: A restore point was created
options.rationale: Creating one is correct; the timing was wrong.

options.text: System Restore stayed off too long
options.rationale: The problem was turning it on too early.

options.text: The user wasn't educated

questions.explanation: Turn System Restore back on and create a fresh restore point only after the system is verified clean.
questions.discriminator_tested: Only after the system is verified clean.

questions.stem: What BEST explains why user education is the final step of malware remediation?

options.text: It prevents the same infection from recurring
It is the last item in the procedure
options.rationale: True, but that restates the question.

options.text: It restores the user's deleted files
It re-enables System Restore

questions.explanation: Educating end users on phishing, safe downloads, and reporting is the final step of the malware remediation process, and it prevents recurrence.
